Subject: Sequence-locked MAP: deployment & region runway for MedSafe (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Ivy / team —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our commitment, I'm kicking off a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to lock the deployment mode and region decision so procurement and engineering have a clear runway. High-level ask: can we land on a preferred initial deployment mode (Hosted US region vs Redwood Dedicated VPC vs Private on-prem) and target a final decision by EOD Nov 16 so we can schedule the pilot/POC work the week after.

Attached: medsafe_map_v2.xlsx (working MAP), preliminary proposal_v1.3.docx, and our security questionnaire stub. Key open items:
- Primary constraint: PHI residency + ingestion controls (Ivy flagged this)
- Latency SLO target: <= 120ms p95 for the interactive flows
- Data flow: which integrations can be proxied vs direct (we'll need network touchpoints)

Proposed evaluation plan (quick):
1) Hosted pilot (US-WEST) for 2 weeks against a scoped traffic profile (low ramp)
2) If latency or data residency blocks are hit, spin up Dedicated pool in customer VPC (us-east) as phase 2
3) Private on-prem only if vendor security/contract gating requires it — longer lead time (4-6 weeks)

Please confirm: (a) whether procurement can accept a short hosted pilot while SOC2 evidence is provided, (b) any non-negotiable compliance constraints that would force Private now, and (c) names for the MAP owners.

Ivy — can you loop procurement on any required legal gating items?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. High level: MedSafe is PHI-heavy and our security council will push for Private deployment unless you can demonstrate concrete technical and contractual controls quickly. A few notes:
- Preferred for now: Private (on-prem) or Dedicated in our VPC (we want control over keys and network)
- We need SOC2 Type II evidence and a completed security questionnaire before any production data is routed to Hosted services
- Procurement: timeline-wise we need term sheet + any redlines by Nov 13 to make the Nov 20 approval window

I'm looping Amir from procurement for the formal timeline. We can do a limited hosted pilot with synthetic data while security evidence is compiled — that would speed the evaluation, but it must be completely isolated and limited in scope.

Ivy / all —

A few technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective:
- Region options: Hosted (us-west-2) or Dedicated pool (us-east-1) — Dedicated gives customer VPC peering, KMS in your account, and private subnets. Private on-prem requires our container bundle + on-prem networking (NAT/egress rules)
- Latency: our baseline for the model family you've selected is ~80-110ms p95 in us-west with the recommended batching profile. Dedicated in us-east will add ~10-25ms overhead depending on the customer's network egress
- Security gating: SOC2 + KMS-in-customer-account will cover most requirements; for on-prem we need a week of validation testing at minimum

Acceptance gates I suggest for MAP progression:
- Gate A (Pilot go/no-go): Synthetic pilot passed (functional & SLO smoke) + security questionnaire >= medium risk
- Gate B (Commit to Dedicated): Gate A passed + procurement term sheet signed
- Gate C (Private): Only if contractual/regulatory prevents Hosted/Dedicated; requires signed ops SLA and on-prem runbook

I'll prepare a short tech checklist and a runbook bulleted doc before the Nov 16 check-in.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
